'''Gimbap''' is a popular snack or lunch dish in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Korea|Korea]]. Its primary ingredients are ''[[Cookbook:Gim|gim]]'' (sheets of dried seaweed) and ''bap'' (rice).

== Ingredients ==
* Yellow pickled [[Cookbook:Daikon|daikon radish]]
* [[Cookbook:Spinach|Spinach]]
* Salt
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|Sesame oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|Sesame seeds]]
* [[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrots]]
* Ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Egg|Eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Steamed Rice|Steamed]] short-grain or sushi [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* [[Cookbook:Nori|Gim]] seaweed
* [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], sausage, or any other kind of cooked meat

== Special equipment ==
* Bamboo gimbap/sushi rolling mat (gimbap mari)

== Procedure ==
[[File:Kimbap feltekerése.jpg|thumb|Arranging fillings in strips]]
[[File:Gimbal (bamboo gimbap roller) 3.jpg|thumb|Rolling up the gimbap]]
# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] radish lengthwise, about 1 cm thick.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] water and add spinach. Boil for about 10 seconds, then drain it.
# Rinse the spinach with cold water, and squeeze all the water out. Season with salt, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
# Shred carrots about 2 inches (5 cm) long. [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|Stir-fry]] it with salt, pepper, and vegetable oil. You don’t have to cook it all the way through.
# Crack about 4–5 eggs into a little bowl. Mix well, and season with salt and pepper. Transfer beaten eggs to a hot greased [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]], and cook like an omelet until it is solid. Cut lengthwise, about 1 cm thick.
# Mix rice, 2 tbsp of oil, and sesame seed together.
# Place the mat on a flat surface and place a sheet of seaweed on top. Spread a layer of seasoned rice on top of the seaweed, and arrange the eggs, carrots, spinach, radish, and meat on top of that in long strips.
# Use the bamboo mat to tightly roll everything up, with the fillings on the inside and the seaweed on the outside.
# If desired, slice the roll into rounds.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Avoid spreading the rice too thick on the seaweed, which will make it hard to roll up.
* Gimbap is good to pack for lunch or a snack, and it makes great picnic food.
